html:
A Greek poet from the island of Lesbos, born around 630 BCE, famous for songs of love and desire. Ancient readers ranked her among the great lyric poets; an epigram attributed to Plato calls her the tenth Muse.

She wrote in her local Aeolic dialect, to be sung to the lyre. Scholars at Alexandria later collected her poems in nine books, but almost all were lost. One complete poem, a prayer to Aphrodite, survives, along with fragments quoted by other writers or found on papyrus in Egypt; new pieces were identified as recently as 2004 and 2014.

Her poems speak of longing for women and girls, of weddings, of her family and of the passing of youth. She lived through political strife on Lesbos and spent some time in exile in Sicily. She was a contemporary of the poet Alcaeus.

The words "lesbian" and "sapphic" come from her island and her name.
sum: A Greek poet from the island of Lesbos, born around 630 BCE, famous for songs of love and desire. Ancient readers ranked her among the great lyric poets; an epigram attributed to Plato calls her the tenth Muse.
